correctness.rationale: A model of the fresh-predicate counterexample sentence has P⊆Q on one domain and witnesses truth changing to false while all other interpretations remain fixed, and every such failure yields a model. In the extended fixed vocabulary there are 2^(k+1) cells. For a rank-q sentence their counts may be taken as 0,…,q-1, finite q, or countably infinite. The rank invariant can be checked with assignments by preserving equality and cell membership and comparing the residual cell counts at the remaining quantifier depth. Choosing a previously assigned element or one fresh representative per nonempty residual cell is enough for ordinary quantifiers; all fresh elements in an infinite cell have the same truth value, and finitely many assigned elements and finite cells can never be infinitely many witnesses. This validates both infinity quantifiers, including their behavior on the empty domain. The vector enumeration and depth-first evaluation require polynomial space for each fixed k, and deterministic PSPACE is complement-closed. For hardness, the guard forces a two-element domain with exactly one P-element, so replacing Boolean binders by first-order binders and atoms by P(x) evaluates the QBF exactly. A true guarded QBF fails monotonicity by expanding P to the full domain, while a false one is unsatisfiable. Guarding the negation of the input, computable by flipping the prefix and negating the matrix, therefore reduces TQBF to monotonicity; extra fixed predicates are irrelevant to the formula. No finiteness restriction or infinity quantifier is needed for the reduction.
residual_risks: Analytical proof and checked reduction, not a machine certificate. The fixed-vocabulary argument gives no bound of the same kind for vocabulary growing with input.

value.rationale: This makes a known semantic test quantitatively precise in the minimum nontrivial vocabulary and for each fixed larger one. It isolates PSPACE hardness to alternating ordinary quantifiers over two elements, while proving that the generalized quantifiers and genuinely infinite models do not raise that fixed-vocabulary bound. That separation is useful for the monotonicity decision problem independently of how original its individual proof ingredients are.
residual_risks: No quantitative claim about producing positive normal forms, practical performance, or input-unbounded vocabularies.
